name: Fourth International–Posadist
summary: Posadism is the Trotskyist current led by J. Posadas after the 1962 split. It holds to world proletarian revolution and defence of the workers' states against capitalism, while criticising their bureaucracies. It is best known for Posadas's view that nuclear war between capitalism and the workers' states was inevitable and could spark revolution, and for his 1968 claim that advanced extraterrestrial civilisations would be socialist.
scope: The Fourth International (Posadist) under J. Posadas, c. 1953-1981, based on the 1968 pamphlet 'Flying saucers and the socialist future of mankind' and scholarly and encyclopedic accounts. It excludes later 'neo-Posadist' internet groups and other Trotskyist currents. Most test statements are not addressed in the sources, so many answers are inferred from Trotskyism and are low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Posadas's pamphlet calls for ending poverty and hunger and giving everyone the means to live with dignity; a socialist state would provide healthcare as part of that, though it is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed; as revolutionary Marxists Posadists back workers' immediate demands as steps toward revolution, but see wages as something to abolish rather than reform.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The pamphlet holds that capitalism, money and profit stunt science and human capacity, so market allocation is rejected in favour of socialism.

public-ownership.rationale: Posadists seek the expropriation of capital and defend nationalised property in the workers' states as the basis of socialism.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not discussed; the aim is expropriating the bourgeoisie, so higher taxes on wealth would be seen as a minor step at best.

unions-good.rationale: Posadas organised a union as a young man and the movement works in the labour movement, but treats unions as arenas for revolutionary politics rather than ends in themselves.

property-fundamental.rationale: The pamphlet describes possessing wealth as a degeneration and private property as the root of narrow human aims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reformist regulation is not a Posadist aim; they want capitalist firms expropriated, so a regulation question is a poor fit and adherents would not prioritise it.

cut-welfare.rationale: A movement aiming to end poverty and hunger through socialism opposes cutting welfare for workers.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialised property under workers' control is the Trotskyist aim, but Posadist texts stress state ownership under a workers' state more than cooperatives.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from a Trotskyist, historically persecuted and banned movement that opposes bourgeois state security apparatus.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Posadist sources do not address drug policy and nothing in them indicates a position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionary Marxists distrust bourgeois state censorship, yet oppose racism, so adherents are not clearly one way.

strong-leader.rationale: Posadas himself ran a highly centralised organisation, but the programme is rule by the working class, not a leader bypassing gridlock in a bourgeois state.

state-harmful.rationale: Posadists want a socialist state after revolution and so reject the claim that the state is unnecessary and harmful; they are not anarchists.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the movement engaged in guerrilla action and favours arming workers, but gun control as such is not a Posadist topic.

empower-police-military.rationale: The bourgeois state apparatus is to be destroyed by proletarian revolution, so more police and military power is opposed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No Posadist source addresses sex work, and I could not find a documented position.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed directly; the pamphlet's picture of socialism as removing the causes of social ills implies rehabilitative rather than punitive justice.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed in sources; Posadas praised childbearing in space as a sign of an advanced society, and Marxists see the family as a historical form, so inferred disagreement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sources I opened say nothing about Posadist views on sexuality, so no position can be documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not documented in the pages I opened; inferred from the broad Trotskyist support for women's rights and social liberation.

more-religion-public.rationale: The pamphlet is materialist and rejects ghosts and spirits as an explanation, so a larger public role for religion is inferred to be opposed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed explicitly; inferred from the stress on ending poverty and oppression worldwide and on the colonial revolution.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources do not address gender theory; adherents' view cannot be documented.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Posadism is internationalist and aims at world revolution, so preserving national culture is not a priority.

gradual-change.rationale: The programme is proletarian revolution destroying the bourgeois state, not gradual reform within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: An internationalist workers' movement opposes restricting immigration, as inferred from its world-revolutionary framework.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bourgeois international bodies such as the UN are seen as instruments of imperialism, so more power for them is opposed; this is inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Posadists reject capitalist markets; free trade is a capitalist policy that they oppose in favour of planned socialist economies.

nation-first.rationale: Posadism is internationalist and aims at world revolution, rejecting putting a national interest ahead of global working-class cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military intervention by capitalist powers is seen as imperialist, so the claim is rejected; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: An internationalist movement would favour eventually open borders, but the sources opened do not state it.

limit-growth.rationale: The pamphlet envisages unlimited growth of social capacity and science under socialism, rejecting limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not discussed; Posadas held that liberated science could end floods and misery, so planned action on nature is inferred to be favoured.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The pamphlet claims that science freed from capitalism could end hunger, floods and misery, and that capacity in socialist society is unlimited.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Posadas championed nuclear weapons for workers' states, yet the pamphlet urges destroying nuclear arms; nuclear power itself is not addressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: The core programme is proletarian revolution and world revolution, and the movement even took part in guerrilla struggle in Cuba.

experts-over-public.rationale: Posadas wanted science freed from financiers and bureaucrats and placed under collective control, so experts do not override popular rule; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Posadists defend the planned economies of the workers' states as superior in principle, with socialism enabling unlimited social capacity.

socialized-markets.rationale: The movement aims at planned socialism, and markets of any form are not endorsed in the sources.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single tax on land is a reform of capitalism, not a Marxist programme, so it is not endorsed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to wealth accumulation suggests support, but expropriation rather than taxation is the actual aim.

basic-income.rationale: Posadist sources say nothing of basic income; they want the end of poverty through socialism rather than a state payment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; defending workers' state economies from imperialism might favour trade protection, but this is not documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A planned economy in which the workers' state directs investment is the Trotskyist model Posadas defended.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The pamphlet treats private property as degeneration; the programme is social ownership, not wide small private ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Posadas envisaged a society beyond class and profit with unlimited capacity, consistent with eventual abolition of money; the sources give no explicit statement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market is capitalist, and Posadists want state control of banking and credit.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class collaboration through state bodies is rejected by revolutionary Trotskyists, who stress class struggle.

one-party-rule.rationale: Posadas attacked Communist parties that do not want to seize power and criticised bureaucracy, yet his own International was monolithic; he favoured a revolutionary party leading but not bureaucratic rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A revolutionary socialist movement rejects hereditary monarchy as part of the old order.

democracy-best.rationale: Posadas refused to ally with liberals to defend liberal democracy against fascism, treating both as bourgeois, so the claim is rejected; this is inferred from early texts.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; revolutionary Marxists prefer council democracy to either referendums or parliaments.

workers-councils.rationale: Trotskyists seek rule by workers' councils (soviets) and Posadas called for a socialist state replacing the bourgeois state; I infer councils from this tradition.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist tradition recognises national self-determination, but Posadas's stance on secession is not documented.

natural-rulers.rationale: The pamphlet envisions everyone becoming an architect, engineer or doctor, rejecting the idea of born rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Posadists backed guerrilla action in Cuba and advocated a preemptive nuclear strike by workers' states, so they reject pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: The pamphlet opposes war and calls for destroying nuclear weapons, though Posadas welcomed a revolutionary war; character-building is not the rationale.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not directly addressed; a materialist movement would favour separation of church and state, inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The pamphlet is materialist and sceptical of spirit explanations, so laws based on scripture are rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private provision of defense and courts contradicts the revolutionary state and public ownership.

military-superiority.rationale: Posadas urged workers' states to hold and use nuclear weapons against capitalism, so military strength of socialist states is valued; this does not apply to capitalist countries.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is internationalist and class-based, so a single-ethnicity nation is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist class struggle as the engine of history is central to Posadism and the Trotskyist tradition.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The pamphlet aims for an end to classes and to poverty, implying equality of condition; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not documented; inferred from anti-imperialist support for oppressed peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Posadas backed colonial revolutions and anti-imperialism, so reparations are inferred to be supported though not documented.

civilizational-union.rationale: A class-based world-revolutionary movement rejects uniting nations on religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The pamphlet attacks wealth-seeking as degeneration and prizes fraternal feeling.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; socialist collective solidarity is stressed, but a duty-over-rights formula is not a Posadist position.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The pamphlet focuses on science mastering nature for humanity; intrinsic value of nature is not discussed.

limit-population.rationale: The pamphlet envisages abundance and praised childbearing in space, so population control is opposed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Posadas expected science and industry under socialism to bring abundance; the disaster claim is rejected.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Posadas supported space exploration and claimed liberated science would transform life; disruption of capitalist institutions is welcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Posadas imagined a transformed humanity with unlimited capacities, but enhancement ethics are not discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Posadas stressed collective thought of society and workers' power, not algorithmic rule; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No documented stance, and this is a modern issue.

restore-past-order.rationale: The pamphlet looks to a socialist future of unlimited capacity, rejecting restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Posadas's writing is strongly doctrinal about historical laws, so judging policies without ideology is rejected; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Posadists did armed action and unions but also formed parties; they favoured revolution through mass struggle, so neither side cleanly fits.

means-match-ends.rationale: Posadas advocated preemptive nuclear attack and ran a centralised organisation, so he did not hold that methods must mirror the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The pamphlet's vision is scientific and technological advance, the opposite of foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Posadas said everyone would become an architect, engineer or doctor under socialism, implying overcoming the division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The pamphlet's goal is to give everyone the means to live with dignity and to end hunger; it does not use the formula explicitly.

production-for-use.rationale: The pamphlet contrasts capitalism's profit motive, which suppresses science, with socialism serving human needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: As Marxists, Posadists hold that capitalist profit rests on exploitation of labour, and the movement's whole aim is to end it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Posadists call for a socialist state replacing the bourgeois one and defend workers' states, in the Trotskyist tradition of proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not documented; Posadas supported regimes with varied land policies, so adherents are not shown to be committed to collective farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement saw capitalism in terminal collapse and expected imperialist nuclear attack on workers' states.

taxation-theft.rationale: A Marxist movement favouring a state-run economy rejects the claim that taxation is theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Posadists do not hold liberal limits on state power; the revolutionary state acts to build socialism; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Marxists treat classes as the main political subjects, so rights belonging only to individuals is rejected.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; workers' states were defended and armed but Posadas's view of conscription is undocumented.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Liberal exit-based freedom is foreign to a movement based on mass revolutionary action.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a revolutionary instrument, not a business serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The pamphlet argues that capitalism limits capacity, and that socialism gives society unlimited capacity, implying freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Posadas stressed capitalist financing of science and the ruling class's power, not media and universities above elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A Marxist internationalist movement rejects racial genetic hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is a corporatist idea opposed to workers' councils.

total-state.rationale: Posadists defended planned workers' states but also criticised their bureaucracy, so a state directing all life including culture is not endorsed.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical national rebirth is a nationalist theme alien to internationalist class politics.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Territorial expansion of nations is rejected as imperialism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath loyalty is the opposite of the revolutionary project.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is rejected by any socialist movement.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The pamphlet claims science is subject to those who finance it, suggesting that knowledge reflects power, though no theory of truth is developed.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist tradition is split on moral universals.

single-common-good.rationale: Marxists see competing class interests rather than a single common good under capitalism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not documented; Posadas backed Arab regimes he called workers' states, and the movement was anti-imperialist, so a Jewish state is inferred to be opposed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No documented Posadist position; this question is a poor fit.

revive-national-language.rationale: No position documented; the movement is internationalist.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' control and democratic management are part of the socialist programme, though a Posadist text on this was not found.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers are a market mechanism opposed to public provision, so Posadists would reject them.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Posadists do not hold orthodox fiscal limits; a planned economy has no such constraint.

economic-freedom.rationale: Posadas held that capitalism limits human capacity and that freedom lies in socialism, not in economic freedom for capital.

rule-by-example.rationale: Posadists envisage state power and organised party leadership instead of moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Trotskyist tradition backs self-determination of oppressed nations; it was part of Posadas's support for colonial revolutions, but his sources do not state it.

force-without-un.rationale: A question about "my country" does not fit; Posadas favoured force by workers' states against capitalism and did not defer to the UN.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The pamphlet appeals to science and reason, though it also speculates about aliens, so confidence is low.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalist workers' solidarity rejects restricting welfare to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not documented; opposed on the basis of working-class solidarity, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Posadas opposed allying with liberals and insisted on class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; Posadas looked toward a new society but not the destruction of libraries and museums.

dominated-front.rationale: Posadas backed anti-imperialist colonial revolutions and regimes in Syria, Egypt and Iraq, so a common front against the West is inferred to be favoured.

workers-nation.rationale: Posadism is explicitly internationalist, organising the working class as a world class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not documented; opposed on general Marxist grounds and the movement's emancipatory outlook.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; Posadists want to abolish capital rather than ban interest on religious grounds.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial segregation is contrary to a class-based internationalist movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist view that the bourgeois state serves the ruling class is basic to the programme of replacing it.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not documented; internationalists reject compulsory assimilation, inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy theory has no basis in a class-based internationalist framework.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; revolutionary Marxists regard electoral systems as secondary to council power.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a national form of government is nationalist; Posadas favoured world revolution not national missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not documented in the sources opened; inferred from Marxist feminism.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The pamphlet criticises capitalist and bureaucratic control of science and Communist parties that avoid power, implying that elites are unaccountable.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy contradicts the movement's emancipatory aims.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not documented; inferred from opposition to the bourgeois state's repression of workers.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Minimal-state liberalism is the opposite of Posadas's planned workers' state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universal equality is implied by Marxist internationalism, though the sources are silent.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Posadas's programme was permanent and world revolution, with socialism requiring revolution in other countries, as Trotskyism holds.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not documented; inferred from secular materialism and opposition to religious law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not documented; a revolutionary movement would not endorse state restriction of conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religion-based ban has no place in a materialist programme.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the movement's materialism.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Posadas defended workers' states yet criticised their bureaucracy; the Trotskyist view favours workers' power rather than a stronger bureaucratic state, so adherents are split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The liberal doctrine of consent is not a Posadist source of legitimacy, which comes from class rule; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is a capitalist national policy contrary to planning and internationalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Expulsion of minorities contradicts the movement's internationalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Posadists advocate revolutionary violence and preemptive nuclear strike, so they reject an absolute ban on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The pamphlet sees capitalism as a brake and socialist cooperation as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The movement was itself banned in Cuba, so it opposes state bans, though it might ban counter-revolutionary parties after power.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept is not discussed; neither side is documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Bourgeois checks and balances are not a Posadist aim; they seek council power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Posadas founded a centralised International and attacked Communist parties that do not want to seize power, implying the need for a revolutionary leadership.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Posadas's pamphlet aims at ending poverty and hunger, though the priority is class power.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Selling off public housing to individuals contradicts public ownership.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are an instrument of working-class struggle.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The pamphlet blames capitalism for poverty and hunger, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Class unity transcends ethnicity in the movement's view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Posadas was a victim of such measures in Cuba, but a revolutionary state would use emergency powers against counter-revolution, so adherents are split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A planned economy and end of hunger implies fixing prices; not documented directly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Posadas criticised the bureaucracy and the Cuban government banned his group, so he stands against bureaucratic control of media, though the revolutionary movement might favour state control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not documented; Trotskyists favour a workers' army under the soviets rather than party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Internationalist workers' solidarity rejects long waits for citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The classical Marxist principle from the Paris Commune, usually shared by Trotskyists; not documented in the pages I opened.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Posadist International was highly centralised and monolithic, with decisions binding on sections.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is seen as a capitalist bloc, though a socialist union of states is favoured, so this is rejected for the EU form.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive control of the military is opposed to workers' council power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; a materialist movement is indifferent or opposed to church governance, inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy is opposed by a materialist socialist programme.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Classical Trotskyist revolutionary defeatism may apply to imperialist wars, but Posadas supported defending workers' states, so it is limited.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not documented; opposed in Trotskyist tradition of cultural freedom, inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocability of delegates is a standard soviet-democracy principle in the tradition, though not found in these sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Posadas favoured alliances among workers' states and the workers against capitalism, so ending alliances is not his position, though capitalist alliances like NATO are opposed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not documented; socialised housing rather than universal home ownership is the likelier aim.

people-in-arms.rationale: Posadists armed guerrillas and called for workers' militias, though no source states it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The pamphlet's modernist stress on science and space contradicts agrarian romanticism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not documented; the movement supported reunification of Vietnam and Korea in practice but sources do not say so.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not documented; the movement stressed workers but did not attack the educated as such.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the stages-of-society framework makes it ambiguous.

death-penalty.rationale: Not documented; opposed in the Marxist tradition against bourgeois state executions, but a revolutionary state might use it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not documented; inferred from emancipatory outlook.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The pamphlet's scientific materialism rejects creationism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship is ethnonationalist and contradicts internationalism.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Leninist tradition supports minority language rights; not documented for Posadism.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Posadas backed anti-imperialist revolutions, and debt cancellation is a standard anti-imperialist demand; inferred from that.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Posadas held that colonial revolutions only succeed when they expropriate capital, as in his labelling of regimes as workers' states.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The movement prefers soviet power to bourgeois assemblies, inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Posadas supported workers' states that restricted freedoms, but he also criticised bureaucracy, so adherents are split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not documented; inferred from internationalism and anti-imperialism.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Posadas argued that nuclear-armed workers' states should keep and use nuclear weapons against capitalism; this applies to socialist states.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Independent central banks serve capital; Posadists want state control of finance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Posadas rejects private property as degeneration, so the conditional justification is not accepted.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Posadists called the Soviet bloc states workers' states, though deformed ones, rejecting the state-capitalist theory.

collective-defense.rationale: Posadas favoured solidarity among workers' states against capitalist attack, so allied defense is in line, but not documented as a rule.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; bourgeois symbolic heads of state are not a Posadist aim.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: No position is documented, and Marxists vary on it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Materialist socialism rejects the sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax is a bourgeois measure that favours the rich.

character-from-environment.rationale: The pamphlet argues that social conditions, such as class society and property, shape human aims, as Marxists hold.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The ruler above law is opposed, as workers' power is meant to be collective.

space-expansion.rationale: Posadas praised Soviet and Chinese space exploration and made contact with advanced alien civilisations a part of his socialist future.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed rule by the few and many is a classical idea alien to proletarian rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Critics called the movement cult-like around Posadas himself, but the programme criticises bureaucratic cults, so adherents would not endorse a national leader cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The pamphlet attacks bureaucracy in workers' states and Communist parties, in line with the Trotskyist view that bureaucracy blocks socialism, though the restoration framing is not explicit.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not documented; inferred from support for peasant-worker alliance and colonial revolution.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is nationalist, and the movement is internationalist.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving religion contradicts materialist and emancipatory aims.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory religious dress codes contradict the emancipatory outlook, inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic union conflicts with class-based internationalism.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Internationalists would favour fighting for rights where they live, though not a documented Posadist view.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is basic to Marxism and Posadas's view of how socialism develops.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is a liberal reform and Posadists want expropriation rather than competition law.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not documented; Posadists oppose capitalism, so they have no stake in either side.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not documented; the question concerns liberal democracy, which Posadas did not defend.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky of a colonial bloc is a fascist-era concept, opposed by Posadas's world revolution.

moral-incentives.rationale: No documented position, and Posadas's texts do not discuss work incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Posadist guerrillas fought in Cuba and the group directed an armed apparatus in 1966, but Posadas later stressed mass action, and the movement shifted away from guerrilla struggle by 1969.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A revolutionary socialist movement abolishes hereditary privilege.

decide-locally.rationale: Not documented; the movement is centralised and internationalist, so maximal localism is inferred to be rejected.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: internationalist Trotskyism teaches history as class struggle on a world scale, not centred on one nation or civilization.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Posadism backed anti-colonial revolution and world proletarian solidarity, and would reject rule by one society over another.

patriotic-education.rationale: A strictly internationalist current opposed to nationalism would reject teaching loyalty to the nation, flag and anthem.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: Posadas centred class, not race, but a Trotskyist current would resist abolishing measures aiding oppressed groups.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Posadas called for the expropriation of banks and a planned economy under workers' states, implying public control of money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Posadas held that capitalism is in terminal crisis and headed for collapse through war and revolution.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: Posadist internationalism opposes imperial claims, though it supported unity among workers' states.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: Posadas backed the planned economies of the workers' states and defended them against capitalism, but called for world revolution, not national delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Posadism held that workers everywhere share one revolutionary interest and called for a world proletarian revolution.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: a collectivist Marxist current rejects property rights as grounds for discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists reject bourgeois constitutionalism and favour workers' democracy; entrenchment against majorities is foreign to this view.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-imperialism: Trotskyist internationalism treats imperial borders as illegitimate impositions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: a revolutionary Marxist current rejects hereditary rule and favours rulers answerable to the working class.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the centralised party model: Posadas ran a tightly disciplined party, which leaves no room for a single dissenter to block a decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: revolutionaries accept removing rulers who betray the people, though they do not ground this in constitutional law.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists look to workers' councils and the workers' state, not bourgeois parliaments, as the supreme authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from Posadas's materialist, science-centred outlook, which holds that human and other intelligence are matters of degree.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from a science-and-progress outlook that accepts use of nature for human needs while favouring less suffering; not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: socialists reject charity from a privileged class as a substitute for abolishing class privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: Posadism is an activist revolutionary party that demands total engagement in the class struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view that capitalist culture and media reproduce bourgeois ideology; Posadas's pamphlet attacks capitalism's hold on science and culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Marxist theory of bourgeois ideology; Posadists also stressed force and the bureaucracy's coercion, so the emphasis is uncertain.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Trotskyist anti-imperialism and theory of imperialism as exploitation of the world's poor by capital.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism, which rejects reserving rights by birthplace.

party-own-road.rationale: Posadism centred on a centralised international that directed national sections, and defended the workers' states, so it did not favour national roads independent of the International.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: Posadas favoured international solidarity and a planned world economy among workers' states, not national autarky.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from internationalism, which opposes revanchist territorial claims between workers' states.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Posadism is class-based, not ancestry-based, and holds that the working class should lead.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the Trotskyist tradition of militant anti-fascism; Posadists did not treat it as a constitutional matter, so the support is mild.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists defend the workers' states and reject equating them with fascism; Posadas defended them against capitalism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist reading of American history, in which slavery was the central cause of the war.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no stake in preserving monuments to condemned figures and would treat them as symbols of the old order.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from a class-first outlook that sees gender-specific programmes as secondary; not addressed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Trotskyist feminism, which treats domestic violence as shaped by social inequality; not addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the universalist claim that socialism is the future of all humanity, advanced civilisations included.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: Trotskyists oppose the bourgeois army as a political actor and seek its dissolution into a workers' militia.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Trotskyist positions on the socialisation of domestic labour; not addressed directly.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources say nothing on family duties and Trotskyists are indifferent to the question; inferred as neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posadism calls for workers' democracy and a socialist state in place of bourgeois institutions, not rule by examined officials; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: A workers' state would hold foreign trade and key industry under state control, so blocking foreign buyers fits; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Trotskyism supports women's equality and easy divorce; inferred from the tradition.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Trotskyist workers' democracy calls for officials accountable to and removable by workers' councils; inferred, since Posadist texts on councils were not found.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The movement wants capitalist enterprises replaced by public ownership, so private pension firms contradict its programme; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Abolishing capitalist property in the workers' states includes land held by the state; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Posadism replaces the bourgeois state with a socialist one and opposes bourgeois parliaments as the source of authority; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Proletarian internationalism opposes forced national languages; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Abolition of capitalist property would end foreign ownership of land; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Marxist analysis treats capitalism as producing structural inequality that must be remedied; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Posadas wanted science and production used for the common good rather than profit, which implies hostility to consumer capitalism; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Posadist guerrillas fought alongside Castro and Guevara in Cuba, and the group supported armed revolutionary movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Posadas defended the workers' states against capitalism, so an intervention to hold a state to socialism is inferred as acceptable.

corporate-influence.rationale: Posadas treats capitalism as ruled by big capital and the state as its instrument, so corporate control of government is a core criticism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; a workers state would restrict capital, but internationalist Posadists would also oppose nationalist sovereignty framing; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from Marxist internationalism and opposition to nationalist local exclusion; a workers state would nationalise property rather than reserve it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the socialist planned economy Posadas advocates, in which work and dignity are guaranteed for all.

democratic-peace.rationale: Posadism sees bourgeois democracy as a cover for capitalism and war, and peace as coming from socialism; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Revolutionaries reject bourgeois law but Posadas demanded a centralised disciplined party; inferred and split.

non-intervention.rationale: Posadists called for the workers states to support revolutions abroad and to defend them against capitalism, rejecting non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trotskyism favours mass workers organisation, and industrial unions fit that; the sources do not state it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Posadism rests on class analysis and internationalism, and rejects ethnic or religious scapegoating.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred as neutral.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Posadas criticised bureaucratic secrecy in workers states and favoured workers democracy; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Posadas favours scientific, planned, international production and socialist abundance rather than localisation; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Posadas built a centralised party and an International and rejected informal organising.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Proletarian internationalism opposes national precedence, though Posadists also reject bourgeois international courts; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Posadism is atheist, internationalist and class-based and would reject defining a nation by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from Trotskyist internationalism, which rejects hierarchies between states, though Posadists defended the Soviet Union as leader of the workers' states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from a centrally planned, internationalist socialism that pools resources across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from standard Marxist doctrine, which separates personal property from the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Posadists defended workers' states and sought world socialist revolution, so they reject defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the demand for state ownership and planning of the economy under workers' control.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from Marxist materialism, which treats religion as a product of social conditions; Posadas's own cosmic claims were framed as materialist.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: As Trotskyists they follow Marx in treating capitalism as having developed the productive forces needed for socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Trotskyism's view that women's liberation depends on socialist transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist programmes that socialise housework and childcare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalism and the absence of nationalist language policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from support for anti-colonial and national liberation struggles and for respecting oppressed peoples' agreements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: Posadists favoured centralised planning in a world socialist system, not small self-governing communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to national chauvinism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Posadas held that the workers' states were the alternative to capitalism, so a third course is rejected.

missingStatements.text: Nuclear-armed socialist states should strike first to destroy the nuclear capacity of capitalist states.
missingStatements.rationale: Posadas argued that workers' states should launch a preemptive nuclear attack, and the thesis is central to his reputation.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic to Posadas; no other ideology would take a side, and it would have to be answered by every future audit.

missingStatements.text: Life on other planets, if advanced, would be socialist and could help humanity end capitalism.
missingStatements.rationale: Posadas's 1968 pamphlet argued that visiting extraterrestrial civilisations must be advanced and so socialist.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic to Posadas; no other ideology would take a side, and it would have to be answered by every future audit.

missingStatements.text: States that abolished capitalist property should be defended against capitalist powers even when run by a bureaucracy.
missingStatements.rationale: Posadists defended the Soviet and Chinese workers' states while calling for the bureaucracy to be overcome.

notes: Gittlitz disputes that a final nuclear war was a settled Posadist doctrine, while the encyclopedic accounts present it as Posadas's view. Primary texts on workers' councils, gender and religion were not found, so those answers rest on Trotskyist inference.
